caption:
Give it one task. Walk away. It keeps working.

In May 2026, Mistral quietly turned its chatbot Le Chat into something else entirely: Mistral Vibe, an AI chat and coding agent built for what it calls "long-horizon work."

The difference sounds small until you picture your actual week. Normally, getting AI to help with anything multi-step means chaining prompts one at a time — write this function, now fix this error, now add this feature, now write the test. Every step needs a new message.

Vibe is built to take the whole job in one go. You hand it an open-ended task and it works through the steps itself, checking back with you instead of waiting on your next instruction.

It's not starting from zero either. It inherits Le Chat's existing strengths — a fast, multilingual assistant with web search, document and image handling, and (since September 2025) memory of your past conversations baked in.

Worth saying plainly: this shipped in May 2026, so independent reviews are still thin. Most of what's public right now comes from Mistral itself, not a deep bench of outside testing. That means early adopters are a little ahead of the reviews — which is also exactly why it's worth being early.

Save this so you don't lose it, and try handing Vibe something you'd normally break into ten separate prompts this week. Full breakdown — link in bio.
